There's a fine line between cozy and tedious. You're helping people decorate their spaces, and find places for all their stuff. But it doesn't really matter. It doesn't matter how you do it, throw it in a big stupid pile, it doesn't matter to the person you're organizing for, and it doesn't matter to the game world, so I just don't care. There's some weirdness that goes on as you explore the town, but I don't care to pursue it further. Is there a great story payoff to doing all the stuff? If not, that makes this game even worse. I admit I didn't care enough to find out, because the "story" is so minimal pasted-on that I didn't have any faith they would pay off more hours of pointless interior decorating.

Whisper Town invites you into a cozy, heartwarming world where decorating, organizing, and uncovering little stories come together in a delightful experience. Taking on the role of the town’s versatile housekeeper, you’ll dive into a variety of charming and quirky tasks. From moving into new homes and tidying up cluttered spaces to setting up fresh shops, sorting through cherished keepsakes, and even tracking down elusive cats, every task offers a sense of purpose and reward. Completing these jobs grants you new furniture and decorative items, giving you the freedom to create a space that truly reflects your style and personality.

As you help the townsfolk bring order to their lives, you’ll begin to notice that your efforts do more than just tidy rooms—they gently influence the lives and stories of the residents around you. Beneath the surface of this quaint town lies a collection of unusual secrets waiting to be uncovered. Every item you place, every corner you clean, reveals traces of the people who live there. The small details—a dusty letter, a carefully placed teacup, a plant resting by the window—each holds a quiet story just waiting to be discovered. Yet, Whisper Town isn’t just about neatness; it’s a playful place too. You might find yourself tinkering with a vintage gramophone, squeezing a rubber duck, or sneaking a tissue from a box, as if the town itself is softly calling out to you through these little gestures.

With over 1,800 pieces of furniture and more than ten unique home layouts, the game offers endless possibilities for personal expression. Whether you want to line a study wall with towering bookshelves, fill a sunlit greenhouse with flourishing plants, or stock a doomsday shelter full of supplies, the choices are yours to make. Customization goes beyond just placement—wallpapers, flooring, and many pieces of furniture can be recolored or retextured to perfectly suit your mood. Dozens of items even feature unique sound effects, so as you explore and decorate, you don’t just see your home—you hear it come alive. Tap the drums, snap a photo, or run the tap to fully immerse yourself in the environment.

Spending time with the townsfolk deepens your connections and builds friendships, enriching the warmth of everyday moments. Yet, beneath the cozy surface, Whisper Town holds mysteries that hint at something more enigmatic. A flickering number—42—hovers above the museum. A sudden rainbow streaks the sky. Rumors swirl about a “heart-stealing ghost” haunting the old well, and strange tentacles seem to creep from cracks in the town’s foundations. These eerie signs suggest that the town’s story is far from ordinary, and perhaps the one destined to uncover its hidden truths is you. Whisper Town balances the charm of simple, heartfelt living with whispers of deeper mysteries, inviting you to explore, create, and unravel its secrets at your own pace.

Rating: 9/10

[list]

[h2] 游戏详评 [/h2]
[h3] 前言 [/h3]
《呓语小镇》是由元气弹工作室制作的一款轻松治愈向的装修收纳游戏，游戏主要玩法为在小镇上装修，打扫各式各样的房间，但是游戏内核却又不止家政。游戏制作精良，steam一经上线就有96%的好评率也足以见得玩家对本作的极高评价
[h3] 背景介绍 [/h3]
欢迎来到呓语小镇，在游戏中主角将作为一位受邀来到小镇工作的家政工，接受来自小镇各处奇奇怪怪的委托，亲手把混乱的房间收拾的整整齐齐，在收拾的过程中可能还会发现埋藏在小镇的种种秘密，比如从床底翻出什么不可见人的物品，从一张画的后面发现隐藏的偷窥房间等等，在委托结束后去抽盲盒来收集各种家具，用这些家具自由的装饰属于自己的空间。享受从普通的家政工做到家喻户晓的传奇家政专家的故事
[h3] 推荐理由 [/h3]
精致的像素画风给人眼前一亮的感觉，游戏细节更是精致，有着大量可互动对话的NPC，街上的大部分东西都有互动效果，玩家可以自由的在小镇上清扫垃圾，修理消防栓，撸猫等等的互动，路边的椅子也像○神一样可以坐下，可以说是细节满满了，更是有着堪称海量的家具数量（1800余种）不爱装修的可能会没那么喜欢，但是对于喜欢unpacking之类休闲摆放的游戏的玩家绝对是可以无脑入手，首发价48.6可以说是相当香了
[h3] 个人感受 [/h3]
解谜和全成就都很简单，没有藏得很深的那种成就，跟着流程基本都可以轻松拿到，游戏的主线不是特别长，大概也就七八小时左右，不过在游玩过程中还可以解锁其他的住宅，可以按照自己的喜好自由建造，除去几个需要按照游戏设定摆放的房间以外，绝大部分主线的房间的摆放自由度都很高，这种就属于千人千样了，每个玩家装修的风格都不会一样，最后呈现出来的效果也肯定是千人千象。强烈推荐房间装修爱好者，强迫症患者游玩，非常值得体验

Reviewing (mostly) every game (or DLC) in my library, part 383:

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️☆ (9/10)

[i]Whisper of the House [/i]is a much better [i]Unpacking[/i]—but with a mysterious, paranormal spin. Suddenly you’re not just organizing a life, you’re uncovering one. As a cozy, home-decor sim, it hits a sweet spot where every dusty corner, mismatched painting, and forgotten trinket feels like part of a secret waiting to breathe. Also, it came out on my birthday, so of course it's going to be great :P

🚪[b] Pros:[/b]
[list]
[*] Cozy decor meets haunting secrets. On surface duty, you’re unpacking, placing furniture, helping clients move in or reorganize, and styling spaces. But there’s always a sense something’s off—hidden rooms, anomalies, whispers behind walls. That duality between comfort and unease is the game’s strongest trick. And then suddenly, you're investigating time travel portals, ghosts, and alien weirdness?!?! This game has more depth than you think.

[*]Creative freedom and satisfying aesthetic. This is the highlight of the game. The requirements are not as strict as in [i]Unpacking[/i]: most missions will let you put items anywhere. And let me tell you, there are so many items in the missions, and even more when you're decorating your (multiple!) houses. There has to be at least 1,000 items in the game. The pixel art is beautiful, as well. And so colorful! The pixel art is rich and textured, every lamp, plant, or shelf feels lovingly crafted. You can tell the difference between regular milk and strawberry milk.

[*]Charming characters and companion robot. Mark, your robot helper, is a delight. Their expressions, little moments of panic when you pick them up by mistake—those touches make the town feel alive. NPCs and clients are simple, but their quirks give personality to the spaces you inhabit, and their designs are very sweet. There's also a guide to everyone you meet, which is very appreciated.

[*]Ambient audio and soundtrack.The music is cozy, but with just enough wistful tension. It's charming for sure. Visuals and sound together make late-night decorating feel evocative. 

[*] Lots of fun and quick achievements that I don't think are missable.

[*] The UI (except for a little nitpick) is very good, especially when searching for items. You can sort by room or by function, and you can search things up by name. I wish, however, that the menus for searching items was bigger on the right side. 
[/list]

📫[b] Cons:[/b]
[list]
[*] My biggest con is that the description text over items is both extremely small and difficult to see. The text is black with a white outline, which creates a hazy effect behind the words. Sometimes the words blend in with the background. The text can def be bigger.

[*] Mechanics sometimes feel clunky. Rotation limitations (you sometimes can't rotate items fully), camera rules (you can’t rotate rooms), and tight spaces might frustrate your interior ambitions. But for the most part, the game is very flexible. 

[*]Translation and dialogue roughness. A few lines feel awkward or stilted, likely due to localization. Some NPC or client text don't flow super cleanly.
[/list]

BUT I have to mention a few nitpicky things that made playing feel tedious more than anything (I still have hopes for the changes tho, this gem deserves to THRIVE) ; 
- The gacha system is a bit off-putting for some sections of the game. It'd be awesome for a slower personal setup of your own place, but it loses its purpose entirely roughly 2-3 hours into the game because you'll have collected enough vouchers to buy everything they offer. Plus it's weird for tasks. First task I ended up with a basically empty room because I had zero fitting items. 
- Speaking of which; the tasks are so confusing sometimes, haha. That might be a me problem but I get so confused and overwhelmed when they request a room and you get an empty apartment like what am I supposed to do here, I don't even have enough furniture to fill it all up. 
- The story feels rushed and I'm disappointed the time machine part was kinda left to rot, I was really looking forward to that in the demo since it felt like such a big deal. :( 
- Please please please let us rotate the rooms, there's so much wasted space and awkward angles for specific furniture because they only turn two ways. 

Still, like I said, I want to see this game groooow. It's still 100% worth every penny.

Whisper of the House -`♡´- es un verdadero cozy game. Lo que más me gusto es lo fácil que es adaptarse: aprendés a jugarlo al toque y los controles son súper intuitivos. 

Algo increíble es que, después de terminar el modo historia, podés seguir jugando. El juego te permite continuar decorando casas anteriores o meterte con las nuevas, un detalle que me encantó porque le da mucha vida útil. 

La estética, el pixel art, la música y los personajes... absolutamente todo está logradísimo.

Un aviso: Recomiendo muchísimo el juego, pero solo si tenés un buen manejo del inglés, ya que por ahora viene en muy pocos idiomas. 

Algunas sugerencias:
[list]
    [*]Estaría bueno que sumen más opciones de traducción.
    [*]Que en los mapas se pueda marcar directamente el local al que querés ir y no solamente la calle.
    [*]A la hora de comprar muebles o comida, sería clave que el tamaño de la imagen previa se mantenga según lo que elegiste antes (aumento o disminución), para no tener que ajustarlo cada vez. 
[/list]

In an increasingly volatile market, within which consumers are expected to satiate executives' greed via microtransactions and expansions, Whisper of the House reminds gamers that pixels do not have to welcome waves of poverty. You will not find a limited edition 1978 refrigerator with an exclusive vinyl wrapping for $1544.99 here, but you can head over to the appliance store and buy yourself an adorable, stylized fridge in a variety of designs. You get multiple residences to decorate freely, as well as gently-guided tasks tidying and rebirthing your town's businesses and homes. You can return to redecorate depending on your current, real season to get seemingly endless time in this sci-fi dipped world. Whisper of the House drips cozy decor, calming atmosphere, and compassionate tales, and it will provide mental sanctuary when you need most. Click one button in your inventory to collect all within a room, breathe, and start again.

A couple notes I had after completing Whisper of the House:
- The description of the cane in the hospital being "usually used by old people" or something along that wording is inaccurate, as canes are used by disabled people. Disabled people can always utilize a mobility aid like a cane, but old people might end up using one eventually. 
- I want to be able to buy mobility aids and other accessibility devices when first starting out, like purchasing any other furniture piece or food item. I want wheelchairs, crutches, walkers, canes, changing tables, talk pads, ventilators, feeding tube equipment, etc. in my little whisper of a world. 
- If customizing your character is introduced, introduction of choosing your character being in a wheelchair or wearing casts/braces to traverse the town would be nice! When I see equipment such as grandpa's chair lift and the hospital's I.V. systems, I feel like I am less alien in my real life, like I don't need to hide my equipment and accommodations, and I feel empowered. But I dream of a future in which kiddos are gifted an affordable, accessible game and actually see themselves alive, welcome, and normal out with the rest of their community.

Posting this for my wife since she played the game via Steam Family Sharing:

Going out of my way to post this review because that’s how much I loved this game!

It feels like the game Unpacking on steroids. Not only do you get to design rooms, but there’s also an active story to follow, a city to clean up, and even a small mystery to solve. I took my time and ended up playing for about 13 hours. Don’t get me wrong, you could probably rush through it in under 2 hours, but the whole point of the game is to decorate, enjoy yourself, and not just fulfill requests as quickly as possible.

It’s the perfect balance: enough gameplay to stay relaxing without ever becoming boring. You can also keep playing after finishing the story, since the notification board updates with new design jobs every day.

PLEASE add more gameplay and objects in the future to give it more of a reason to play after finishing the story, because this really has the potential to become one of my most favorite games of all time.

I have no complaints, really. This game is definitely worth the price for how much content is in it. I like the 'gacha' format for getting furniture, it's actually quite fun since it isn't hard at all to get the in game currency or collect said furniture. I love the option to have multiple home bases to decorate as well. 

I will say sometimes, some homes or buildings have decor items that should fit in one area that don't, and it starts to feel awkward placing things where they realistically shouldn't go (such as the bakery or some of the convenience stores). This is a very small thing however. 

The visuals are really cute, and i love the little stories you get inserted in per building. The granny who had passed was my favorite, discovering more about her, her cats, and so on. I also love that there's magic and supernatural stuff inside, it makes the whole game feel really whimsical. After playing Unpacking, I was really sad to learn they weren't making any more levels or content. However, this game easily filled that void for me. If you like Unpacking or any game similar, I think you'll definitely like this one.

This game is both relaxing, puzzle solving, and entertaining. You get to go around a cute little city and help people either clean up their flats or unpack for them, meanwhile you get several houses of your own to freely design and decorate with found and purchased (in-game money only, no real money spent) items. There are smaller hidden themes and puzzles, but overall very relaxing with no time-constraints.

Absolutely LOVED this game and I'm hoping for more updates so I can keep playing! The storyline is cute and a little spooky at times, the decorating tasks are so fun, and it's simple enough to play. Also love that there's plenty of free time to just design your own home(s) throughout the game!

When the creators of Unpacking said they had no intention of making a follow up game, I was stung. This game soothed that burn. It's relaxed, comforting, and highly interactive. I beat the main story and still have some little areas to work on, which I fully intend to do. I deeply enjoyed this game. With that being said, yes I'm going to be that person. It would have been nice to have a customized character. There really isn't a reason why we have to choose between two genders and one skin tone in 2025. It could have just been pick the body frame, pick the skin tone, pick the hair, and be done with it. That was my only hang up with this game. That, and a tiny bit more guidance could have been given.  However, this game easily paid for itself.

The puzzles weren't too hard, I didn't have to look anything up, and figuring out everything was very satisfying.
I would rec this game to fans of Unpacking - that's what I thought it might be like, and I was right!

通关全成就+全图鉴打卡

累鼠我了终于集齐了，整体主线时长差不多4 5个小时，但是后续找全成就和全图鉴又花费了好几个小时，不过整理收集癖大满足！
一开始冲着类似《Unpacking》的玩法来的，《Unpacking》是整理收纳类游戏永远的白月光，这个游戏比《Unpacking》更自由开放一些，有多条故事线，同时也增加一些玩法的变种，以及大世界的探索，总之还是很好玩的，如果《Unpacking》是9分，这个可以7分。
要吐槽的地方：
公告板任务做的很重复很无聊，而且对于做成就毫无帮助
仓库分类做的很混乱，不明白这个分类的逻辑是什么，建议增加个自主分类的功能
精心给某几个房间做了装修但素不能分享感觉很可惜啊啊啊，希望有个联网观看他人装修成果的功能，可以互相点赞！

最后希望以后可以继续更新和优化，多一些主题房间~

止め時がなくて、うっかり徹夜しそうになってしまった…
図鑑コンプしたり、自分好みの部屋を作るやりこみもあるのでこの手のものが好きならぜひ。

クリアまでプレイしました。
まず、おすすめしますか？を『はい』にしましたが、かなり人を選ぶゲームではあると思います。
自由に、もしくは言われたとおりに、さらには掃除もしつつ要望に合うようになどなど、様々な状態で部屋の内装を配置していきます。ちまちまと配置していくだけという作業に心地いい音楽。眠くなる人は眠くなるし、没頭できる人は没頭できる、そんなジャンルのゲームです。
私はちまちまお片付け作業が好き（ゲームの中に限る）なので、とてもハマりました。

そんな作業は大変楽しかったのですが、残念な点もあります。
ゲームの流れ的には片づけをしながら町の住民のそれぞれの物語をなんとなく知っていく？という感じなのですが、そこがどうもぼんやりふんわりつかみどころのない表現。
日本語化にありがちな意味のありそうで無い日本語が入り組んでおり、若干理解が難しいところがあります。
これは私の文章読み取り力が足らないのか、皆がそうなのかは分かりません。
もちろん分かる所は分かるのですが、クリアまでプレイした最後に総括して「なるほど、わからん。」でした。

ストーリーはひとまず置いといて、可愛らしい雰囲気と素敵な音楽。
そしてとにかく片づけ作業が楽しかったので結果としては買って良かったゲームでした。

I rarely leave reviews, but this game really was something!

The story is well written and rather long, there's atleast 8-10 hours worth of story gameplay, and the rest can be used to re-decorate or decorate your own houses, it's a very lovely game and it had a few surprises up it's sleeve! 

I highly recommend getting it, but please note that the story doesn't last forever, and to truly enjoy it try take it at a slower pace, instead of cramming through the entire story in 1-2 days like I did.

It does feel a bit lacking in some areas, such as options when it comes to decorating your own home, interacting with people and so forth, but nothing too limiting. 

I do also wish you were able to fully customize your character, rather than having to pick between a blonde boy or a black haired girl, and being able to actually own a pet, after seeing so many of them in the game.

It's definitely a good game for those who want to sit back and relax and just organize things though!

这是一款像素风的装修收纳游戏。

游戏的画面是像素风格，有一个比较大的地图，小镇的场景虽然小人细节少了一点，但是建筑看着还是很不错的，而进入到房间内部的时候，建模的精细度就更高了，而且有不少物品和家具都有互动，总体来说画面表现还是非常不错的。

游戏的背景说的是玩家受小镇镇长的邀请来小镇当家政工帮小镇居民处理搬家，收拾等事件。然后玩家在完成各个委托的时候发现了小镇上各种隐藏事件，比如房间里的密室，帮助进入高维的炼金术士重返小镇，通过时光机器拯救疯狂科学家的爷爷之类的小事件。

最后得知镇上的博物馆馆主居然是外星人，由于玩家帮助解决了小镇的各种异常，外星人在把控制小镇时间和天气的能力交给玩家之后，驾驶飞船离开了小镇。

总之设定还是比较大杂烩的，科学，魔法，幽灵什么的都有，当个乐子就行，并不影响具体玩法。

玩法上其实就是类似Unpacking那种收纳，整理房间的玩法，玩家接受委托之后，带着机器人从大地图进入指定的房子，然后从机器人的包裹里拿出物品在对应的房间摆放。

除了某些特定的委托需要玩家按照要求摆放指定的家具，其他的其实都是可以随便乱摆的，哪怕乱扔一地，或者你自己的都觉得不好看，但其实完全不影响玩家完成委托。

完成委托之后可以获得点券，可以在各个商店抽盲盒获得家具，之后这些家具可以用来装修因为完成委托而获得的各种房产。

房子装不装修其实都无所谓，属于锦上添花，通关和成就里都无对应的要求，全看玩家喜好。

通过需要在各个委托和大地图上找到并收集异常，数量还是非常多的，而且还有一些解谜和剧情在里面，总体体验还是很有趣的。

博物馆只需要收集42个异常就能通关，但是异常总数远远高于42，所以不影响通关，通关之后，玩家可以继续探索其他异常进行全成就收集，看地图上还有很多地块是被挡住不让走的，估计后续是能出DLC的。

[h1]温馨小镇下的汹涌暗流，家政工拯救世界！——「呓语小镇」[/h1]
《呓语小镇》是一款像素风解谜游戏，定档8月27日正式上架Steam。玩家在游戏中扮演一位家政工，来到这个温馨的呓语小镇，但是却嗅到了一丝异常的味道......玩家要做的就是完成委托要求的所有内容，在这个过程中，你也许会发现一些小秘密。

[h2]家政工的日常[/h2]
家政工这个职业其实在现实中也很常见，甚至可以说每个地区都有从事这个工作的人，工作的内容也很庞杂，主要就是完成雇主提出的任务，细分下来有打扫卫生，收纳整理，搬运家具等等。在游戏中玩家扮演的主角隶属于一个搬家公司，核心工作内容就是上门摆放家具和打扫卫生。

小机器人马克会协助玩家工作，点击机器人就可以拿出家具，再进行合理的摆放。当然不乏有雇主对摆放的位置有特殊要求，根据他们的指引完成即可。

一间房子中会有好几个房间，比如卧室、厨房、卫生间、客厅等等，每个房间都有一个单独的进度，放置家具可以增长进度，达到100%后就代表这个房间装修完成了。将全屋全部达到100%就算完成任务啦。

除了放置家具外，主要工作内容中还有一项打扫卫生，有的顾客希望翻新房子，玩家右键点击污渍清扫，点击破损的家具可以将其拆分成废材，最后将所有垃圾和废材全部扔进垃圾桶就完成任务啦。值得一提的是，垃圾桶设计的很可爱，如果试图将不是垃圾的东西扔进垃圾桶，那么它就会说“请不要投喂垃圾！”，好像也没什么问题，毕竟对它来说垃圾才是美食。

最后，完成任务的同时还需要击碎这个小镇中的异常，异常可能潜伏在任何物品上，症状也比较明显，散发着紫色光芒，不断向外扩散奇怪的符文，并且伴有轻微抖动。右键疯狂点击就可以击碎异常，使被附身的东西恢复正常。

[h2]小镇的故事及个人体验[/h2]
背景故事中，玩家来到呓语小镇从事家政工，但并没有这么简单，在玩家来之前就有一座神秘的凭空金字塔出现在小镇中，奇怪的是人们无法进入期内，唯一的可疑的点只有金字塔上闪烁的一个数字，除此之外再无其他的线索。

主角在完成家政任务中击碎异常后，金字塔上的数字就会变少，这代表了什么？数字清零后是否可以进入金字塔了呢？金字塔内到底有什么呢？这些就不剧透啦，小伙伴们自行探索哦~

地图上可以探索的东西很多，小摊贩，自动售货机，杂物堆等等都可以探索。玩家完成家政任务后会获得代金券，代金券可以去抽取家具，家具可以用来装修自己的房子或者打造样板间。后期完成大卖场的任务后也可以直接进入其中购买指定家具，就不需要随机抽取了，不过抽卡也是别有一番乐趣的。

[h2]个人玩法与感受[/h2]
完成特定的雇主任务后，玩家会获赠房屋，玩家可以在这些房间中用获取的家具进行装修，多套房子可以使用多种风格，发挥你的想象力和主观能动性，数千种家具可以搭配出无数种方案。

游戏整体还是比较治愈的，画风很可爱，虽然是像素风格但是非常精细，地图上包含的内容很多，绝对不是滥制粗工。

游戏中对于人物的刻画也很细致，只要深入探索就可以发掘很多NPC身上发生的故事，儿时的梦想，亲情的桎梏，友情的美好等等。

这里就要夸夸游戏的支线了！支线通常是不会直接告诉玩家的，玩家在完成家政任务中会遇到NPC，细心一点的对话后再去完成NPC的请求就可以完成支线，很多支线藏得很好，通常三顾其而不知都是可能的，这也侧映了游戏很耐玩，有太多未知的事务等着玩家探索呢~

[h2]写在最后[/h2]
其实还是有点反差的，在一开始我只以为是一款轻松治愈的经营模拟类游戏，没想到游戏中竟然还包含了解密和拯救世界的要素，该说不说确实使游戏变得更加有趣耐玩了，谁能拒绝做一个大隐隐于市的拯救世界的英雄呢？妥妥的漫威主角剧本。

游戏中获取家具的方式包含抽奖和直购，照顾到了几乎所有玩家群体，我个人就很享受抽奖的过程，基本都是去抽取的。但也不排除有的小伙伴被抽卡折磨得毫无体验，所以游戏中还设置了直购，免除抽卡的繁琐。

最后希望小伙伴们享受家政工的琐碎日常，用心去发现和装饰美好的明天~

[h2]Finally more unpacking[/h2]

Games like this are always going to be compared to unpacking from now on, I don't think unpacking was the first game like it, but it was definitely a game that perfected the format, storytelling via organisation and decoration, since playing this game, it's actually helped me to better understand why unpacking is as limited as it is.

There's a certain vibe to unpacking, I don't know if it's in the music, or the colours, or the fact you never see another person outside of your scrapbook, but this game didn't [i]quite[/i] capture it, and that's not bad, I want to make that abundantly clear, while I do want those same unpacking vibes I had when I first played it, and this game comes closer than pretty much any other game I've played since, this game is branching out doing it's own thing, and in doing so, it sets itself apart from a game like unbox the room for example (although clearly both games have differing levels of time, effort, and manpower put into them).

By picking up on the different vibes of a game like unpacking versus whisper of the house, it made me realise that while a community levels mode for unpacking would be phenomenal, it may not quite capture the same atmosphere as the base game, it helped me to understand why something that sounds simple enough, may be a lot more complicated to do well, and I appreciate this game for helping me develop that understanding, because while I feel the same about what unpacking should've had in addition to the base game, I feel like I have a more defined view of what that'd take, and why it's a bigger challenge (beyond technical limitations and having to rebuild the game from scratch).


Now that I've got that out of the way, I want to get onto this game and give it the praise it deserves, instead of just going on about one of it's predecessors.


Whisper of the house has a couple of rough points, some friction between what the player wants to do and believes they can do, stacking certain items they can appear to float a bit, some things which logically should fit where you're trying to place them may not quite fit, certain draws, cupboards, or fridges can't be opened, and perspective mode is incredibly easy to miss, and just assume "oh, I've put something where I can't get it back, it's just stuck there forever now", and potentially even believe you've soft-locked yourself because of where you've placed something, not realising you can get it back.

I love the idea of that sort of semi-open-world thing they're going for, but it does feel a bit barren and small after some exploration, there's just not a whole lot to do, maybe some minigames would be nice a couple moments focusing more on character interactions probably wouldn't hurt, being an event organiser for example, setting up the venue for a party on the beach, I don't think the "hub world", for lack of a better term, hurts the game at all, I think it's important for the identity the game has, but I do kind of wish there was a bit more to it, maybe that's a bit beyond the scope of what they're going for here though, I don't know.

Having sort of puzzle game and mystery elements incorporated into the levels works pretty well, most of them are executed pretty solidly, but by the end I felt kind of dissatisfied, I just felt like it was building to more of a climax, but there wasn't really one, maybe that's on me, maybe I got the wrong idea, but the creepy letters and anomalies, I just felt like there should've been more to it, I think if this game gets consistent content updates though, maybe expanding the town, it could become one of the modern greats of cosy gaming, I think awareness and maybe a couple elements of it's execution are the only things holding it back, I know this might be unrealistic, but a co-op mode could be fun, decorating a house together, or walking through the town together just looking around, it'd certainly help the town to feel a bit more alive if there was someone else in it with you.

If there was any 1 criticism I could give, I'd say it's absolutely that the town needs to feel more alive, maybe in a way along the lines of a short hike's world and characters, while I didn't hate any of the characters, they didn't feel all that compelling to me, the first couple levels I was like "oh this is cute", and receiving that "hey you should come hang out sometime" text I was like "aww that'd be so nice", maybe something like stardew's heart events could be incorporated to help build those relationships with the characters, and really breathe some life into them, rather than purely serving as exposition for why you're unpacking stuff in this place.

Unpacking really thrived with it's storytelling, but it got off easy by only focusing on a couple characters, really only 1 and her life, and limiting dialogue to a couple lines she writes in her scrapbook, to be able to have the same emotional weight or compelling characters, with the route this game has gone down, it needs to do more legwork to have that same effect, and that's not to say the game absolutely MUST have it, but I think it'd benefit from it.

Ultimately the game is still great as it is, I'd like there to be more, I'd love content updates, fleshing out the world, more levels, community levels, community towns even, but I think as it is it's pretty solid too, I'd [i]love[/i] more, but if that's not gonna happen, I'm still happy with the game as it is, and I think it's worth playing for any fan of cosy games, or anyone who enjoyed unpacking and wanted more, just don't expect anything identical, comparisons are fair, as I said, they're going to happen with any game like this for as long as people keep playing it, but understand that this is it's own game, it's doing something different to unpacking, and give it the respect it deserves for that, because I have so much respect for this game and the team behind it for what they've managed to do here.

In [b]Whisper of the House[/b], you play as a professional housekeeper in the pixelated "Whisper Town."
You primarily receive letters from neighbors and help them with various tasks.

[u]Organising and Unpacking:[/u] Moving furniture and arranging personal belongings.

[u]Cleaning:[/u] Tidying up cluttered spaces to make them livable.

[u]Exploration:[/u] You walk through a living town, visit shops, and interact with many unique NPCs.

As you organise, you’ll notice "anomalies"- strange glitches with flickering lines, objects that shouldn't be there, or dark secrets hidden inside the walls!

You eventually unlock and decorate your own home, using the furniture you've collected from jobs and the catalogue is [b]MASSIVE![/b] There are over 1,800 items to collect and use.

Personaly, since I was a big fun of the UNBOXING (2021) I loved the idea of an open world with the ability to decorate not only houses but also shops.
The game gives you a relaxing, "lo-fi" aesthetic combined with a slow-burn sense of unease.
There were, however, some cases where the transitions from cozy decorating to searching for anomalies can feel disjointed.

So, I've rolled credits on the main story.  I gotta say, I did enjoy my time, though I feel there's more mystery than explanations.  Now, that, for the most part, is NOT a bad thing.  I don't need everything explained.  I liked that some puzzles were present without you realizing they were there.  [spoiler] Shout out to the alchemy puzzles and knowing Ian was missing and the page of instructions. [/spoiler].

Though others, I'm fairly sure there is something to do I'm just not sure where to look for the answers.  [spoiler] The runes you get in the graveyard have several of us stumped. [/spoiler].

I felt the music and sound were fine.  Music didn't overly stand out, in a good or bad way and the sounds were what you'd expect.

I'm a big fan of decorating/placing furniture and having some spookiness with that was rather fun.

The main story isn't a LONG game and I'ms sure you could speed run it if you felt like it (some jobs are longer than others, or easy to get away with little, mostly the bulletin board ones) so factor that in with your decide to purchase or not.

Like I said, I've rolled credits and there IS more to still do so I'm pretty satisfied.

看画风本以为又是一款大同小异的像素风轻松休闲小游戏，没想到《呓语小镇》真的不一般。

游戏中玩家的身份是一位刚刚搬入呓语小镇的房屋装修师，承担着为小镇居民们装修房屋的责任。基本玩法就是根据居民们的要求，将所有大大小小几十件功能不同定位不同的家具一一安放在它们最好的归宿里，譬如洗漱用品安放在卫生间，电脑游戏机安放在书房等等。看似平平无奇的玩法却因为本作在细节方面拉满使得整个游戏过程极其有趣享受，首先就是家具们只规定了房间的要求，具体如何安放完全取决于玩家自身的审美和设计；其次就是家具拆分得可以说是无微不至，单是一张床铺就可以由床头木板、床垫、被子、枕头等等四五个部件构成，其他像是先安放茶几桌子再在上面摆上诸如花篮抽纸等杂物装饰自然也不在话下；另外家具们都有着自己的备注，既有趣又在一定程度上提示了应该放的位置。

作为装修师除了给居民们干活我们自然也可以装饰自己的房屋，通过完成任务可以赚取货币，货币可以用来在商店里购买各种各样的家具盲盒，从而给我们简朴的小屋打造成一个奢华的小天地！

然后就是在小镇的探索，小镇的许多地方都可以互动，譬如可以把垃圾扫掉，获得奖励；收拾地上没人要的纸箱子，发现一些小装饰品……

并且本作其实还有着隐藏的主线，在这些温暖的日常背后，玩家会发现小镇似乎并不平静：突如其来的彩虹、井底的“掏心鬼”、缝隙间伸出的触手……当然还有博物馆上空闪烁的“宇宙的终极答案”42，这些奇异事件的出现也以另一种方式逼迫、驱使着玩家不断往后探索，给予了玩家一个动力和目标。

总而言之无论是被画风还是被玩法吸引来的玩家，本作都可以说极其出色，休闲型趣味性拉满的同时也有一定剧情上的探索性。

才玩了两个多小时，但是迫不及待给好评！世界真的需要更多像呓语小镇还有unpacking这种类型的游戏啊！对上了我这种在现实中懒得收拾屋子，游戏中却乐此不疲的人的电波。很符合我的胃口，都不太舍得玩了（🥹害怕会结束 ）每次看到小屋被收拾得整整齐齐都会有满足感和爽感
                                                                                          
优点：
1.这款游戏对比unpacking，对于物品的摆放没有特别多要求，玩家能根据自己的习惯更自由摆放物品，还会很贴心的展示每个物品的功能和名称（在物品提示中也有很多幽默的梗哈哈，心领神会了），不会有unpacking那种因为不知道是什么东西来回尝试的抓狂感了。
2.故事设置在小镇里，不同的人物登场，之间还会有关联。小镇有很多建筑物，给了玩家更多探索的空间，有很多情节和彩蛋都会在你探索的过程中一点点发现。
3.更让人惊喜的是，还包含了恐怖（？）元素，平静的小镇透露出淡淡的诡异感，总觉得背后会有阴谋。4.像素画风和美工真的好看很治愈，喜欢！     

改进:
1.希望能像双点医院那样可以转换视角看房间                                                                            2.我们需要更多的内容啊啊啊啊啊！
豪玩，很适合那种静下心来东跑跑，西走走的休闲玩家，装修很上头，就是给我的户型有点烂说实话，能不能给个超级大浴室，我要狠狠泡澡。

Full Walkthrough: https://youtu.be/aAC_gNuQxsE
Gameplay: Very Good
Story: Good
Music: Good
Graphics: Retro
Game Time: 4.5 - 9 hours
